verses.text: These are the wise sayings of Solomon. Solomon was the son of David, and Solomon was king of Israel.
Wise Lessons for Life will help you learn to be wise, to accept correction, and to understand wise sayings.
Wise Lessons for Life will teach you to develop your mind in the right way. You will learn to do what is right and to be honest and fair
Wise Lessons for Life teach people who know very little to be wise. They will teach young people what they need to know and how to use what they have learned
A wise person will listen and gain more learning. A person with understanding will get good guidance.
These Wise Lessons for Life will help you understand wise sayings and what they mean, the words of wise people, and the hidden meaning behind their sayings.
Respecting the LORD is where knowledge begins. But foolish people look down on wisdom and discipline.
Son, listen to your father's instruction, and do not abandon your mother's teaching.
Your father's instruction and your mother's teaching will be like a beautiful wreath on your head, like a fine necklace around your neck.
My son, if sinners try to lure you into sin, do not go along with them.
If they say: Come with us, let us hide and wait to attack someone and spill blood. Let us hide and ambush an innocent person for no reason.
Let us swallow them alive, like the grave swallows people. Let us swallow them whole, like those who go down into the pit.
We will find all kinds of valuable things, and we will fill our houses with what we have taken.
Join us and share what we get. We will all share one moneybag together.
My son, do not walk in the same path with them. Keep your feet away from their path.
Their feet run to do evil, and they hurry to spill blood.
It is useless to spread a net where a bird can see it.
But these men hide and wait to ambush their own blood. They hide to attack their own lives.
This is what happens to everyone who is greedy for unfair gain. It takes away the life of the person who has it.
Wisdom calls out loudly in the street. Wisdom raises her voice in the public square.
Wisdom cries out at the noisy street corners, at the entrance of the city gates. Wisdom says:
How long will you simple people love being simple? How long will mockers enjoy mocking, and fools hate knowledge?
Turn and listen when I correct you. I will pour out my thoughts to you. I will make my words known to you.
I called you, but you refused to listen. I reached out my hand, but no one paid attention.
You ignored all my advice, and you did not want my correction.
So I will laugh when trouble comes to you. I will make fun of you when terror strikes you —
when terror comes on you like a storm, and trouble comes on you like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish overwhelm you.
Then they will call out to me, but I will not answer. They will look for me, but they will not find me.
This is because they hated knowledge, and they did not choose to respect the LORD.
They did not want my advice, and they rejected all my correction.
So they will eat the fruit of the way they chose to live, and they will be filled with the results of their own plans.
The simple people will be killed because they turn away, and foolish people will be destroyed because they feel safe and satisfied.
But whoever listens to me will live safely and will be at peace, without fear of harm.

verses.text: My son, if you accept my words and treasure my commands within you,
So that you pay close attention to wisdom and set your heart on understanding,
If you call out for insight and raise your voice for understanding,
If you search for it like silver and look for it like hidden treasure,
then you will understand what it means to respect the LORD, and you will find the knowledge of God.
Because the LORD gives wisdom; knowledge and understanding come from the LORD's mouth.
The LORD stores up sound wisdom for honest people. The LORD is a shield for those who live with integrity.
The LORD guards the paths of justice and protects the way of his faithful people.
Then you will understand what is right, fair, and honest — every good path.
When wisdom enters your heart, and knowledge is pleasant to you,
Good judgment will protect you, and understanding will keep you safe.
Wisdom will save you from the way of evil people, from those who say twisted, dishonest things,
From people who have left the right paths to walk in dark ways,
Who enjoy doing evil and take pleasure in the twisted ways of wicked people,
Whose paths are crooked and whose ways are dishonest.
Wisdom will also save you from another man's wife, from a woman who is unfaithful and flatters you with smooth words,
Who has left the husband of her youth and forgotten the promise she made before God.
Her house leads down to death, and her paths lead to the dead.
No one who goes to her ever comes back; they never find the path of life again.
So walk in the way of good people, and stay on the paths of the righteous.
Honest people will live in the land, and people of integrity will remain in it.
But wicked people will be cut off from the land, and those who betray it will be pulled out by the roots.

verses.text: Better to be poor and honest than to be a liar and a fool.
It is not good for a person to be without knowledge. If you hurry and do something too quickly, you will make mistakes.
People destroy their lives when they do foolish things, then they get angry and blame the Lord and say it is his fault.
When someone is rich, they have a lot of friends, but if he becomes poor, he has no friends.
A false witness will be punished, and someone who tells lies will not escape.
Everyone wants to be friends with an important person. They also want to be friends with someone who gives away gifts.
A poor man's brothers do not like him, and his friends will avoid him even more. When he really needs them, they stay away from him. There is no one there to help him.
To obtain wisdom is to love yourself; those who do what they have learn shall do good
A false witness will be punished, and someone who tells lies will not escape.
It is not normal for a fool to be rich or for a slave to rule over princes!
A wise man does not become angry quickly. He always wants to forgive the mistakes of other people.
The shouts of an angry king are like a roaring lion, but his kind words are like the dew on the grass.
A foolish child brings a lot of trouble to his father and a complaining wife is like the constant dripping of water.
People receive houses and money from their parents, but a good wise wife is a gift from the LORD.
A lazy people wants to sleep all day, and someone who will not work will not have any food to eat.
People who obey the commandments of the LORD will live. But he that ignores God’s ways shall die.
Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and he will reward them for what they have done.
Discipline your children while there is still hope. Avoiding it because of their crying will end badly for them.
A person who gets angry quickly will always have trouble. If you help him, you will have to help him again and again.
If you listen to what people teach you and you learn from them, you will have wisdom in the end.
People make a lot of plans about what they want to do, but the advice of the LORD will endure.
The most important thing that you want from other people is for them to kind. It is better to be poor than to be a liar.
The fear the LORD and you will have a good life, one that is satisfying and protected during trouble.
A lazy man puts his hand in the bowl to take food, but he is too lazy to bring back his hand to his mouth.
If you punish a mocker, the simpleminded will learn a lesson; if you correct the wise, they will be all the wiser.
Children who would steal from their father and chase away their mother are a child that causes shame and bring disappointment.
My son, if you stop learning, you will turn your back on knowledge.
Using a criminal as a witness makes a joke of justice. Sinful people love to do things that are wrong.
Judgments are prepared for mockers, and stripes for the back of fools.

19.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Fixed several typos and grammar issues.

verses.text: Wine is deceiving, and alcohol causes fighting; everyone led astray by them lacks wisdom.
People should be afraid of an angry king, like they are of a lion that roars. If you make the king angry, you can lose your life.
It is an honor for people to stop from strife: Any fool can start an argument.
Because of the cold a lazy person will not prepare their fields: then in the summer they shall beg for food, and no one shall give to them.
Getting information from someone can be like getting water from a deep well. If you are wise, you can draw it out.
There are many people who say: ‘You can trust me.’ But there are only a few of them that do what they promise.
Good people live in the right way and are honest. God blesses their children who live like they do.
When a king sits on his throne to judge people, he separates out all evil with his eyes.
No one can say, I have made my heart clean, have never done anything sinful.
The LORD hates people that use the wrong weights and measures to cheat others.
Even children show what they are like by the things they do. You can see if their actions are pure and right.
The Lord has given some people ears to hear and some people eyes to see.
Do not love excessive sleep, or you will become poor; Open your eyes so that you can do your work and you will be satisfied with bread.
When a person is buying something, they always say, “It's no good. It costs too much.” Then they go away and tell others what a good deal they got.
There is gold, and an abundance of jewels; But the words of someone who is wise are even more precious.
Take the garment of anyone who puts up collateral for a stranger; hold it in pledge if he does it for an unfamiliar woman.
If you have cheated someone to get food, it will taste good in the beginning but in the end, The guilt and consequence will be bitter.
Get good advice before you make your plans. Before you start a war, ask for the advice of wise advisors.
A gossip goes around telling secrets. Don’t be friends with someone who does not care what he says.
Those who would curse their father or mother are like a lamp that goes out in the darkest night.
If someone gets money that he inherited too quickly, when he is too young, It will not be a blessing in the end.
Don’t say, “I will get even for this wrong.” Wait for the LORD to handle the matter.
The Lord hates people who cheat when they weigh things and who are dishonest
No person knows what will happen to him. It is the Lord who decides what will happen to us.
Think carefully before you promise to give something to God. Later, you might wish you had not made that promise.
A king who is wise can find out who is guilty and punish those who have done wrong.
The LORD gave us our mind and conscience; we cannot hide our thoughts and doings from Him.
Mercy and truth protect a king, and his throne is made secure by mercy.
We admire a young man for his strength, but we respect an old man for his gray hair.
Sometimes it takes a painful experience to make us change our ways.

20.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Fixed several typos, a duplicated phrase (v9), and a garbled verse (v28) that had drifted from the actual meaning of the Hebrew.

verses.text: These are the wise sayings that King Lemuel’s mother taught him:
My child, I am your mother. I prayed to God and He gave you to me.
Don't waste your strength or your life on women. Do not give your efforts to things that destroy kings.
Lemuel, kings should not drink wine, Or for rulers to desire strong drink.
If they drink too much, they will not remember the laws and will not be able to judge the people in trouble rightly.
Alcohol is for the dying, and wine for those of bitter of heart
Let them drink and forget their troubles. Let them forget about all their suffering.
Speak up for people who cannot speak for themselves. Help people who are in trouble.
Speak for them and be fair when you judge, and protect the people who can not help themselves and who have nothing.
A wife of honest character is hard to find. She is worth far more than rubies.
Her husband trust her. He will never have to steal because he is poor
She does good for her husband all her life, and she never brings him trouble.
She gets wool and flax and enjoys making things with her hands.
She is like the merchants' ships; she brings her food from far away.
She gets up while it is dark and she prepares food for her family and for the servants who work for her.
She looks carefully at a field and buys it and she plants the vineyard
Her arms are strong, and she keeps on working.
When she sees people wanting to buy the things that she makes, she works all night.
She makes thread with her hands, and she weaves at the loom and makes clothes.
She loves giving to poor people and those who can not protect themselves and who have nothing.
She does not worry about her family when it snows because they all have warm clothes.
She makes blankets and her clothes are made of linen and purple wool.
Everyone knows her husband. He sits with the leaders of the land at the gate.
She makes clothes and sells them, and she gives the merchants sashes to sell.
She is a strong and a neat woman, and people honour her. She is not worried about what will happen.
She always speaks words of wisdom, and she teaches her people to be friendly.
She oversees the care of her house. She is never lazy.
Her children respect and praise her, and her husband says she is a good wife. He says:
'There are a lot of good women, but you are better than all of them.'
A woman does not always stay young and beautiful, but you should always praise a woman who serves and fears the Lord.
She must get the reward for her hard work, and everyone in the city must praise her.
